ai.title: Disable WebSocket protection in non-production environments
ai.summary: WebSocket protection middleware now skips rate-limiting checks when `env.ENVIRONMENT` is not set to production. This change prevents development friction by allowing unrestricted WebSocket action matching during local testing. The update applies to `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts`, specifically within the `protec.use` handler chain.

eli5.text: You: If you're testing the app locally or on a staging server, you can now open as many WebSocket connections as you want without being slowed down or blocked by security checks. The system automatically skips the usual rate-limiting protection whenever it detects you're not running in the live production environment. This only affects development and testing, real users on the production site still get the full protection.

ai.title: CLI diff command added
ai.summary: CLI now supports `diff` and `d` commands to print last assistant file changes. Implementation tracks `lastChanges` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, rendering green/red diffs via `handleDiff`. `SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS` updated in `common/src/constants.ts` to include `diff`. System prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` enforces file verification before edits.

eli5.text: When you interact with the assistant and it makes changes to files, you can now type "diff" (or just "d") to see a quick summary of what files were added, changed, or removed in the last response. The changes appear in green for additions and red for deletions, so you can review exactly what the assistant did. This works right away, there's also a note in the menu explaining the new command, and the assistant's instructions now make sure you only edit files you've actually been shown before.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.83
ai.summary: Bump npm-app/package.json version from 1.0.82 to 1.0.83. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: The product label was rolled forward to mark the release that is already shipping this week. Updating to this version gives you the new pricing page behavior, simplified credit displays, broader tool detection, relaxed real-time checks outside production, and the new command for reviewing the assistant's last file changes. If you pull this release you get those items; sitting on the old label keeps missing them.

ai.title: Simplify CLI diff header display
ai.summary: CLI diff output now prints a plain hyphen before file paths instead of green text. This removes color formatting from the `lastChanges` loop in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Scope limited to CLI diff rendering.

eli5.text: When you run a command to see what files changed, each changed file name now appears right next to a simple hyphen (-) instead of in colored text. This only affects the list you see in your terminal when checking recent changes, so the difference is purely visual. The change has already gone live.

ai.title: Disable OpenAI store flag
ai.summary: Commented out `store: true` in `promptOpenAI` call within `backend/src/openai-api.ts`. Simplified error logging in `promptOpenAIWithContinuation` to pass raw error object instead of extracting message.

eli5.text: The system that powers the assistant's responses has stopped saving copies of those conversations to a database for later review. Anyone using the assistant today would not see their chats stored or reviewed afterward, and if something goes wrong, the error details shown to internal monitoring will be more raw and less cleaned up. This change is live now and only affects how conversations are handled behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix logger context leakage in mixin
ai.summary: The `mixin` function in `backend/src/util/logger.ts` now returns a shallow copy of the async storage context (`{ ...loggerAsyncStorage.getStore() }`) instead of the direct reference. This prevents mutable context objects from leaking across log entries, ensuring isolation between different execution contexts. The change applies to the backend logging subsystem.

eli5.text: When your assistant writes log entries, it used to accidentally let details from one conversation seep into the next, causing log entries to get jumbled together. Now, each log entry gets a clean copy of the conversation details, keeping things tidy and isolated. This affects the background system that records activity, and you wouldn't directly notice it unless you were checking the logs themselves.

ai.title: Auto commit staged changes in CLI
ai.summary: Added autoCommitChanges method to CLI class. Checks for staged changes via git diff --staged --quiet. Commits with message 'Manicode: auto commit' if changes exist. Called before staging new changes in stageAllChanges.

eli5.text: The CLI now quietly saves your in-progress work before starting a new batch. When you run the staging command, it first checks whether anything is already waiting to be committed; if it is, it commits that work on your behalf with a standard message before adding the new changes on top. This only affects people running this CLI tool directly, you won’t see a prompt, the commit just happens behind the scenes. It’s live today.

ai.title: AI commit message generation for autoGit
ai.summary: Added `generate-commit-message` action to backend and CLI to replace static auto-commit messages with Claude Sonnet-generated summaries. New `common/util/git.ts` helpers handle staging and diff retrieval, while `npm-app/src/cli.ts` integrates async generation into the `autoGit` flow. Websockets in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts` route staged diffs to `generateCommitMessage`, returning imperative-style commit texts to the client.

eli5.text: When you run the auto-commit command, the software now asks an AI assistant to write a clear, human-readable summary of your changes instead of using a boring, generic message. The AI looks at what files were modified and generates a short description following standard commit conventions. You would notice this if you use the command, as your git history would suddenly have meaningful descriptions of what actually changed rather than generic placeholder text.

ai.title: Fix applyPatch hunk index fallback
ai.summary: patch.ts adds maybeStartIndex guard in applyPatch. Prevents negative or out-of-bounds startIndex from corrupting getMatchIndex. Falls back to undefined when startIndex < oldIndex. Internal core utility refactor.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to apply a text change to your file, it now double-checks that the starting position it calculated actually makes sense before using it. If the position turned out to be negative or past where the matching text was found, the tool stops trying to guess and safely skips that step instead of getting confused. You won't see this happening, but it prevents rare cases where a patch could be applied to the wrong spot in your file, so edits land more reliably behind the scenes.

ai.title: Refactor git utility functions and improve CLI output
ai.summary: Refactored `common/src/util/git.ts` to separate staging from change detection, introducing `hasStagedChanges` and updating `stageAllChanges` to return a boolean based on the new helper. Silenced `console.error` in `getStagedChanges` and added a try-catch block to `commitChanges` to prevent crashes on empty commits. Updated `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to use `hasStagedChanges` for auto-commit logic and adjusted newline placement in CLI output messages.

eli5.text: The tool now checks your work more carefully before saving changes and gives you friendlier messages about what it did. When you ask it to save your progress automatically, it uses a sharper test to see if there's actually anything new to save, and it no longer crashes if you try to save an empty batch of changes. If you watch the messages appear, you'll notice the blank line now shows up before the explanation instead of after it, making the text easier to read.

ai.title: CLI change display and commit message output
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to prefix added lines with `+` for file changes and removed green coloring from auto-commit message output. This improves diff readability by explicitly marking additions and ensures commit messages render in standard terminal color.

eli5.text: When you run the tool's change report in your terminal, newly added lines of text now appear with a clear + marker in front of them, so it's easier to tell what was added versus what was already there. The automatic commit message that gets printed at the end of a save now shows up in the normal terminal color instead of green, so it blends in cleanly with the rest of the text you see. You don't need to do anything differently, just notice that additions are more clearly labeled and the final message looks slightly less highlighted.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.84
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.84. Updates package.json in npm-app.

eli5.text: Your AI coding assistant will now write commit messages about your changes using a newer, smoother model that summarizes what you did in clearer language. The version label was simply bumped to reflect this batch of updates, which also includes a slightly cleaner look when the assistant shows you file differences and a few under-the-hood bug fixes that make it more reliable in the background. These improvements are now live for everyone using the assistant today.

ai.title: Fix installer detection on Windows
ai.summary: Installer detection in `npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts` now uses `where` on Windows instead of `which`. The change adds a platform check for `process.platform === 'win32'` and wraps the execution in a try/catch block to handle errors gracefully. This ensures correct path resolution for `manicode` across different operating systems.

eli5.text: On Windows computers, the program that finds where helper tools live now uses the right command for that operating system instead of the one meant for Mac and Linux. This means Windows users will no longer hit errors when the software checks which tool (like npm, yarn, or pnpm) is installed. If you watched the installation process on a Windows machine, you would no longer see error messages about detecting the installer location. The change is live today and affects only the internal detection step before any helper tool runs.

ai.title: Add 5MB file size limit to project file reading
ai.summary: Enforces a 5MB limit on files read by `getFiles` in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped and replaced with a `[FILE_TOO_LARGE: ...]` placeholder string to prevent memory issues. This change applies to the core file reading logic used by the agent.

eli5.text: If you're working on a project with very large files (over 5MB), the system will now skip reading those files completely instead of trying to load them all at once. You'll see a placeholder message like '[FILE_TOO_LARGE: 7.32MB]' in place of the actual file content, so you know the file exists but wasn't processed. This prevents the system from running out of memory when dealing with giant files, and it only affects the core tool that reads your project files - everything else works the same.
